newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares rebound, but off intra-day high.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares rebound, but off intra-day high.

text.p: Shanghai B shares rebounded on Friday mainly due to the strong performance of Pudong shares, but ended off their intra-day high of 54.054 points, brokers said.
The index rose 0.603 points or 1.14 percent to 53.421 points, on volume of 14.3 million shares worth $6.3 million. Of 42 B shares, 40 traded, with 24 up, eight flat and eight down.

Brokers said Shanghai B shares rebounded after Thursday's losses with institutional support for the market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development, but off the intra-day high on profit-taking and overseas unwinding selling.

Shanghai Lujiauzui experienced a volitale day, testing an intra-day low of $1.000 on heavy overseas selling, but domestic support made it end up $0.020 or 1.86 percent at $1.090. It was the most heavily-traded stock on volume of 1.5 million shares.

Local media said on Friday that Premier Li Peng had attended a ceremony in the Pudong development zone on Thursday to launch a project for the design and production of integrated circuits, involving investment of more than 10 billion yuan.
"Domestic investors were seen buying Pudong shares, but profit-taking and unwinding selling emerged late in the session," one broker said.
"There was heavy resistance around 54 points with overseas institutions reluctant to buy at current levels with little sign of improvement in firms' results," another broker said.
"The market will consolidate around 52 points early next week if there is no market-moving news at weekend," he added.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere was the star on institutional support in order to help its planned issue of more B shares, up $0.030 or 7.14 percent to $0.450 on volume of 816,000 shares.
Shanghai A share index rallied on capital flowing in from the Shenzhen market, and the market is likely to rise further, brokers said.
The Shanghai stock exchange extended the trading time of A shares, funds and treasury bonds by 30 minutes on Friday because of technical problems on the trading system, exchange officials said.

The A index jumped 43.083 points or 4.13 percent to 1086.081 points, on volume of 1.1 billion shares worth 9.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 86.327 points or 3.46 percent to 2581.906 points.
Harbin Swan was the star on institutional buying, surging 1.30 yuan or 21.43 percent to 7.59 yuan on volume of 11.2 million shares.
